newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh economy to grow at seven pct - report.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh economy to grow at seven pct - report.

text.p: The Bangladesh economy, helped by steady macro-economic development, is expected to grow by seven percent a year from 1996-2000, the official BSS news agency said on Monday, quoting an United Nations survey report.
The report was released in Dhaka on Monday by ESCAP (Economic and Social Council for Asia and the Pacific) on Monday.
Bangladesh's central bank said earlier this month that the growth rate in 1996/97 (July-June) was expected at 5.5 percent.

"The present investment rate in Bangladesh is 16 percent of Gross Domestic Product. The current conducive atmosphere has also brought better prospect for its agriculture and foreign investment. All these will help the country to attain seven percent growth annually," Dr A I Aminul Islam, a UN consultant, was quoted as telling reporters.

The report praised Bangladesh for carrying out wide-ranging monetary and fiscal reforms and for successfully containing inflation from 10 percent during 1981-90 to just over four percent over 1991-95 period.
"The most recent trends indicate that inflation to stabilise at that level (four percent) or to come down further," the report said.
The report said Bangadesh's export growth rates as a percentage of GDP had jumped from six percent in the 1980s to nine percent in 1990s and had grown faster than imports.
But the report slammed poor coordination among the country's instititons, which it said constrained policy implementation.
It also said infant mortality remained high as quality of healthcare and access to the service were severely limited for large number of people.
The report warned that continued overcrowding of agriculture in Bangladesh would lead to further rural-urban migration.
The number of people living in urban areas was expected to double from 18 percent in 1995 to 36 percent by 2020.
